content.summary_of_the_paper:
In this paper, a dual-domain optimization deep-unfolding framework is proposed, which integrates the strengths of both (1) image-domain and (2) convolutional-coding-domain priors. The experimental results achieve state-of-the-art performances.

The performance improvement is too limited and many techniques have been exploitted before.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
The experimental results on natural and MR image CS tasks achieve state-of-the-art performances.

Weaknesses:
1.The novelty of this paper seems limited, and many ideas appeared in the prior works, ie, ISTA-Net, ISTA-NET++ and DCDicL as mentioned in section 3.4.
2.In the contribution, the authors claimed that the proposed framework can be easily applied to other inverse imaging problems, but there is no corresponding experiments to support this.
3. The authors claimed convolutional-coding-based DUNs can transmit high-capacity informative features among stages, however the initial convolutional coefficients α and the convolutional dictionary D are all learned by an E2E way, which means there is no additional information brought into the network during training. The constrain that projects the original signal into high-capacity feature-level image representation seems can also be achieved in the image domain by more hidden layer channels (more parameters). It does not have insights. I suggest authors can give more convincing motivation (e.g, theorem, experiments) to explain why such operations are used.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
This paper is well organized and has good presentation and reproducibility.

The key issue the the novelty is too limited, especially compared with ISTA-Net, ISTA-NET++ and DCDicL.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The key issue the the novelty is too limited, especially compared with ISTA-Net, ISTA-NET++ and DCDicL.
Also the performance impromvent is too limited. 
I recommend  the authors to pursue other path for image inversion.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper addresses the problem of compressive sensing reconstruction. In particular, it proposes Dual-Domain Deep Convolutional Coding Network that integrates the merits of both image-domain and convolutional-coding-domain priors to constrain the feasible solution space. The dual-domain constraints could achieve more accurate recoveries than single domain constraints. Experiments on two datasets demonstrate the superiority of proposed method compared to other methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
+ Fairly easy to read the paper, the authors do a good job presenting the background and literature review on the subject.
+The proposed framework is technically sound.

Weakness:
- Experiments are not sufficient. Table 1 only shows the comparison with MADUN, other state-of-the-art methods should be included.
- Experimental results are not convincing, particularly the CS-MRI reconstruction problem. The difference between different methods can hardly be observed in Fig. 8 and Fig. 9. The real dicom image is recommended to use as experiment data, not the png image. FastMRI challenge dataset would be a good choice.
- Inference speed should be compared between different methods.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The author mentions the source code with pre-trained models of their proposed method will be made available.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper is well written and easy to read. However, experiments are not sufficient enough, inference time and model parameters should be compared with other competing methods. There are a lot of components in the unfold stage, analysis and importance of each component are missing thus not convincing to readers.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an algorithm that improves deep unrolled networks for compressed sensing reconstruction. Traditional networks successively apply a gradient step followed by an anti-aliasing step to remove artefacts from the gradient step. This work instead estimates the image, as well as a dictionary and dictionary coefficients for the image. In order to do this, the authors use various variable splitting techniques, as well as ADMM steps to allow parallelism.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Weaknesses:
- The methadological innovation is a little weak. The prior work MADUN proposes running an unrolled network on the convolution coefficients, while this work proposes splliting the image as well as convolution coefficients and running the unrolled network on both. The modules for each optimization step are fairly standard tools, and it is hard to argue its innovation.

- The numbers in the tables make little sense without confidence intervals. The SSIM and PSNRs are already very close to one another, and the statistical significance of these results are not obvious.

- MoDL is an algorithm from 2017, and the choice for using that as the only established MRI baseline for table 3 is unusual (I've never heard of MADUN before, and the choice of this as a baseline seems arbitrary). Why not compare to something that's established, such as E2E-Varnet? The numbers also do not match known quantities -- MODL does not achieve .90 SSIM at a 10x compression factor.

- The performance of MADUN and this work seem unnaturally good given that they're trained on 100 MRI images (as stated in section 4.4). What was the test set? Was it different from the training set? Were the hyperparameters tuned on the test set itself?

Miscellaneous:

- This is a minor nitpick, but the introduction seems to claim that DUNs are the best choice for CS reconstruction, based on the fact that other deep learning methods "lead to the extreme difficulty of analysis". DUNs don't allow easy analysis either, even though they may be the preferred family of algorithms among practitioners.

- The name dual domain is very confusing -- I guess the authors want to say that they are optimizing two params (hence the word dual), but this is in direct conflict with dual variables in an optimization sense.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is well written and coherent. The name dual-domain optimization (there is no dual variable, the authors are optimizing over two variables instead of one) is confusing and needs to be changed. 

The originality and novelty have some issues -- the techniques are standard reshashes of existing modules in deep unrolled networks.
content.summary_of_the_review: The main concerns about this paper are around its technical novelty as well as the experimental evaluation. The optimization techniques are largely borrowed from prior work on unrolled reconstruction networks, and the statistical significance of the results is questionable. The major baseline considered is MADUN, which is a somewhat arbitrary choice.
